differences.what: massing: a stone town house with a full-height swell bay rising from the raised basement to the wall head, a narrow entrance strip north of it, and its south side wall in shade along the driveway; the draft stood a grey flat-roofed box
differences.how: T-2420, moved to 1621 by T-2440: K01 frontage on the 1911 sheet's plan of 1621, a K02 smooth limestone front, the K08 bow on the sheet's 2.3 m chord and 1.02 m rise at the south end of the front, rising from grade to the cornice; through the plate's one station point the bow's south edge lands about 7 px from the drawing's, its top within about 5 px, and its north edge about 57 px right of the drawing's (the bow's width, below)

differences.what: bow lights: two a storey either side of a central pier in the principal and second storeys, tall, under flat heads
differences.how: T-2420, narrowed by T-2440: two K06 two-over-two sash a storey at -30 and +30 degrees on the bow, 0.75 m wide (the drawing's are about 1.1 m: two such lights overlap on the sheet's 2.3 m chord), their heads and sills the drawing's, within about 15 px

differences.what: storey lines: the principal floor at the stoop's head, the second floor at the bow's string course, the wall head at the bow's top
differences.how: T-2420: a 1.4 m principal floor and 3.9 m storeys; through the camera, carried unchanged to 1621, they fall within about 15 px of the drawing's bands

differences.what: the roof storey: the drawing lights it with a steep pedimented WALL GABLE rising from the wall over the bow, about 3.4 m across, with three short segment-headed lights under radiating voussoirs, a horizontal cornice, a raking cornice round a recessed pediment panel, a finial at the apex and two pinnacle shafts at its foot; T-2420 built a single-light pedimented dormer set on the hip in its place
differences.how: T-2428, moved and narrowed by T-2440: the K05 dormer as a wall gable (dormer.wall_gable), its face on the wall's plane 0.45 m north of the bow's centre as the drawing sets it, three K06 segmental lights under seven-stone voussoir blocks, K10's cornices, a recessed pediment panel, a turned finial and two square pinnacles. Its heights are the drawing's (the pediment's foot within about 5 px, its apex within about 10 px); its width is 2.5 m against the drawing's 3.4 m, its lights 0.55 m against 0.75 m and its pinnacles 3.1 m apart against 3.8 m, so that the pinnacles stand on the sheet's narrower front and the gable's valley clears the crow-stepped south wall: about 20 px narrower each side through the camera

differences.what: the roof behind: the drawing slates a steep roof whose south parapet steps up from the front in crow steps to a tall stack; the build has a 45-degree slate hip (the K01 contract's steepest) with plain eaves and two stacks against the south wall
differences.how: T-2459, moved by T-2440: K01's gable roof, the street slope at 45 degrees to a ridge along the front 4.23 m back at 13.43 m, and the house's south side wall carried up as a five-step crow-stepped parapet to a level head at 13.73 m and a 0.9 m stack rising in the wall's plane to 15.03 m. At 1621 the stack stands 0.62 m behind the ridge, clear of the narrower front's wall gable; through the camera its top lands about 12 px under the drawing's and about 30 px left of it, and the steps rise from the cornice to the stack as the drawing's do, now from a corner within about 10 px of the drawing's, since the sheet's 1621 has no wide pier south of its bay

differences.what: the cornice: the drawing runs a moulded stone cornice at the bow's top that carries the balcony, and across the front at the same line; the build hung K10's bracketed timber cornice under the eave, with the bow stopping under it at 8.2 m in a plain timber eave
differences.how: T-2460, moved by T-2440: K10's moulded stone cornice swept along the street front under the K05 soffit (8.24-8.6 m) and round the bow's top as its own eaves, one moulding; through the camera it lands within about 10 px of the drawing's

differences.what: the balcony: an iron (or turned) rail round the top of the bow; the build's bow ends in a plain deck
differences.how: T-2525: an iron rail on the bow's moulded cornice, 0.06 m in from its edge and round the bow from the wall to the wall: a post against the wall at each end, a foot rail and a top rail, square bars about 0.08 m apart, 0.6 m high (the drawing's rail stands about 29 px over the cornice's top at about 48 px a metre). Through the camera its top lands within about 5 px of the drawing's at the bow's front, and its bars read about as close-set as the drawn ones; it runs across the sheet's narrower bow (the widths, below)

differences.what: the entrance: a recessed round-arched doorway with voussoirs in the north strip, and over it at the second floor a small ornate light above a carved panel; the build has a flat-headed panelled door under a K09 hood and a plain sash over it
differences.how: T-2526: K07's deep-arch door, a round-headed hole 1.2 m wide with its crown 2.7 m over the landing, a pair of panelled leaves under a radial fanlight 0.32 m back in the wall, under a block of voussoirs cut in the front's stone and radiating from the arch's centre, 0.3 m beyond it; through the camera its crown lands about 7 px under the drawn one (485 px against 478), its spring about 3 px, and the opening about 7 px narrower than drawn. Over it at the second floor a light 0.75 m by 0.95 m, its sill 1.2 m over the floor, in K09's restrained surround (architrave, frieze block and cornice hood on consoles), its head and sill within about 2 px of the drawing's and its hood within about 5 px; under it, on the belt course, K09's carved foliate panel, within about 5 px of the drawn panel's top and foot and about 11 px narrower

differences.what: the entrance arch's outline and depth: the drawing turns its voussoirs to a curved extrados under a band and sets the door at the back of a recess deeper than the wall, its jamb lit inside; the build cuts the voussoirs out to a rectangular block in the coursing and sets the door 0.32 m back in the 0.45 m front
differences.how: T-2531: K07's deep-arch entrance laid with a curved extrados (`entrance_kit.arch.extrados`): each voussoir cut between the round head and a ring 0.3 m beyond it, standing 0.04 m before the wall, the block's spandrels laid flush in the front's stone, and over the crown a band 0.15 m deep laid as one more belt course (4.4-4.55 m); the door at the back of a recess 0.95 m deep, K07's own reveal for the variant, whose vestibule carries it past the 0.45 m front. Through the camera the band lands about 5 px under the drawn one (about y 468 against 463), the ring's crown within about 5 px, and the recess's lit north jamb reads about 20 px wide against about 25 px drawn (a reveal inside the wall gave about 6 px). L-k01-1621-last-drawn-2531

differences.what: the light over the entrance: the drawing seems to stand it a little proud of the wall on a moulded shelf over the carved panel, with returns at its sides; the build sets it flush in K09's surround, with K06's sill under it
differences.how: T-2531: K09's `shelf`: the light and its surround stand 0.08 m before the wall on a stone tablet as wide as the surround's seat, its sides the returns, over a moulded shelf of two stepped courses 0.3 m deep under its sill (the upper 0.16 m proud), and the carved panel hangs from the shelf's foot as the drawing draws it. Through the camera the shelf's foot lands within about 2 px of the drawn one (394 against 392) and its top about 8 px under it, the build keeping K06's sill on the shelf where the drawing seats the light on it directly. L-k01-1621-last-drawn-2531

differences.what: the stoop: the drawing's climbs beside the strip, parallel to the front, behind a stone cheek; the build's is a straight stoop toward the street
differences.how: T-2530: K07's side stoop (`entrance_kit.side_stoop`): the door opens on a stone landing running south along the north strip from v 1.0 to the bow's north junction at v 3.6, 2.4 m deep and faced to grade, and from its south end the K01 stair's eight equal risers (0.175 m, on 0.28 m goings) run on south parallel to the front, 1.2 m clear of it so that the 1.2 m flight passes in front of the bow, down to grade at v 5.56, behind a solid stone cheek on the street side whose top rakes 0.1 m over the nosings; the foot opens south. The plate's inset plan draws the steps' nosings square to the front, the steps south of the landing and in front of the bow's north end, between it and the enclosing cheek. Through the camera the landing's street edge runs from x 152 to 287 at y 610 against the drawn landing line's 137 to 277 at y 593 (about 15 px right and 17 px low), and the cheek rakes from (281, 605) down to (385, 670), high at the north and falling south at about the drawn cheeks' slope (0.63 against 0.58-0.65), but about 100 px right of them: the drawn flight stands in front of a 1.4 m strip beside a 3.7 m bow, and the build's leaves a landing that has to reach from the middle of the sheet's 3.6 m strip to its 2.3 m bow, so it passes in front of the bow (the front's widths, below). The iron rails the plate draws over the stoops at the left of the panel are not legibly this flight's, and none is built. L-k01-1621-side-stoop-2530

differences.what: the basement: two segmental-headed lights under the bow with iron grilles, about 0.9 m high; the build's bow is blind in its basement (the K08 kit refuses a light under a bay's clear wall)
differences.how: T-2525: the bow's basement built as a storey of its own, 1.4 m to the principal floor, so the bow carries the string course the drawing draws there; in it two lights at -30 and +30 degrees under the principal lights, 0.92 m high over a 0.1 m plinth, their heads flat as the drawn openings are (the drawing's arch is the grille's, not the head's), each barred with seven iron uprights between a foot bar and a head bar and the arched ring the drawing draws over them, as a plain ring. Through the camera their heads land within about 3 px of the drawing's and their sills about 9-10 px above (the drawing takes them nearly to grade, under the kit's plinth and sill stone); they are 0.75 m wide as the principal lights are, against about 0.95 m drawn (the widths, below)

differences.what: the basement lights' heads: the drawing sets a block of splayed voussoirs over each, its joints fanned up to the string course; the build's are K06's plain flat lintel
differences.how: T-2531: K08's `voussoirs` on each basement light: five dressed stones from its head to the bow's string course, the block 0.08 m wider each side at its top, their joints fanned, each 0.04 m proud with a 0.015 m chamfer so the joints read. They are 0.19 m tall against about 0.3 m drawn, under the build's string course, which stands lower than the drawn band (within the storey lines' 15 px). L-k01-1621-last-drawn-2531

differences.what: the front's widths: the drawing draws a north strip of about 1.4 m beside a bow of about 3.7 m (its inset plan puts the strip at about a third of the front); 1621's 1911 sheet traces a 6.2 m front, 3.6 m of it north of a 2.3 m bay at the south end, so the build's strip is about 45 px wider at its outer edge and its bow about 57 px narrower at its north edge. The sheet controls the plan (the survey of what stood nearer the scene, against the 1886 design)
differences.how: argued in the camera's solve and docs/RESEARCH/hamline-1621-2436/README.md (T-2440): either the bow was built narrower than drawn or the sheet's bay is a later one, and no picture after 1886 is known to say which; the plan is built to the sheet and the heights to the drawing; the stoop's place follows from it (T-2530): the build's flight stands about 100 px right of the drawn one because its landing reaches from the middle of the sheet's wider strip to the sheet's narrower bow

differences.what: the pier south of the bow: the drawing carries the bow to the south corner; K01 keeps a bay 0.3 m clear of a corner, where the sheet draws it about 0.1-0.2 m off (about 7 px at the corner)
differences.how: the kit's minimum pier, within the trace's own precision; T-2440

differences.what: storey count: the 1911 sheet prints '3B' over 1621, three storeys and a basement; the drawing shows two full storeys over a raised basement and a third in the roof under its gable, which is what is built
differences.how: T-2440: at 1621 the sheet's '3B' and the drawing agree (at 1619 the sheet's '4' did not), the roof storey counted as the third

differences.what: colour and tone: the drawing is a monochrome pen plate
differences.how: the stone (Bedford limestone), brick and paint are reconstructed, L-k01-1621-hamline-front-2440; the 1911 sheet reads 1621 'brick' and does not mark the stone front the drawing draws

differences.what: the walk and the front boundary: the drawing brings the side stoop down onto open ground before the house, no fence, wall or gate across the front; the build had lawn-less bare ground and no walk
differences.how: T-3221: the front built open (form.boundary layout open, carried to 1904 on this drawing) and a flagged walk laid from the flight's foot, its 1.2 m width, straight out to the public walk; the drawing hatches the ground and shows no walk's line or material, so its flags and line are the K14 kit's (L-k14-walks-1600-block-3215)
